title: Spirit of the Spear
text: That night? The night I spoke with Ark, was it? In any case, this looked exactly like someone impersonating Rival’s form. No, I say—it was clearly someone else entirely!
“Who are you, I say! What do you intend to do, locking me up in a place like this!”
“Oh? You noticed pretty quick. But ‘who are you’ is awfully cold, considering I’ve been keeping you company this whole time…”
The thing wearing Rival’s skin answered me with an unsettlingly chilly smile.
“I’d appreciate a little respect from the guy I’ve been putting up with through his bizarre driving style, you know.”
“Bizarre, you say! That is a high-speed movement style for a loving rendezvous with Filo-tan, I say!”
Did it have some complaint about my drive mode! But what did it mean by “putting up with”? My memory felt strangely hazy. Had I met something like this fake Rival somewhere before?
“Same old obliviousness. Well, I suppose in your world nothing less would be forgiven.”

I tried to piece things together from the surrounding circumstances. And then it suddenly came to me—the story of how, when Father collapsed from Takt’s attack, he’d had a conversation with Tiger Girl.
“You are…”
“Yes, well guessed. Your thoughts are an open book. We’ve been together for quite a while now, nano.”
Rival’s form wavered and vanished, and in its place appeared something like a ball of fire.

“Nice to meet you… no, that’s not quite right, is it. I’ve spoken to you many times, and you’ve answered back now and then, so since we’ve already been communicating, maybe ‘nice to meet you’ is the polite thing to say anyway.”
“Are you… the spirit of the spear, I wonder?”
“That’s right. This is the deep realm of the spear. Well, since we’ve come this far, care for some tea?”
And with that, a low table and tea appeared out of empty space.
“I can bring out anything you put into the spear before crossing worlds. Is there something you’d like?”
“I don’t need anything, I say.”
“Really? Well, if you say so.”
Looking more closely at the wavering fireball, I could make out the silhouette of something lizard-like in its shadow. A salamander, perhaps?

“Now then, knowing you, you’ve probably forgotten, so let me fill you in—right now is after your lifespan ended, in the continuation of the parallel world where the heroes worked together to overturn the conspiracy and went to the country called Faubrey.”

Hearing that, I remembered… indeed, this was after I’d spent a peaceful lifetime with Father and the others. Countless things had happened since then too, and every day had been joyful. The memories were hazy, like mist, but I could recall them.
“When you move on to the next branch, they’ll be purified within you and some of it will fade, but—did you manage to remember?”
I nodded silently.
“I understand you’re the spirit of the spear. So what business does the spirit of the spear have with me, I wonder?”
“Well, let’s just talk. You’ve finally remembered that day, after all.”

Come to think of it, that was the cause of my looping again, wasn’t it. A measure to prevent me from returning to the original world, forgetting Filo-tan and Father and the others, and descending into the hell of endlessly romancing pigs.
“The things Ark and Ho-kun did for me, I take it.”
“Yep. It’s a request from Sensei Ark, after all. I’ll stick with you to the very end.”
“Sensei, you say?”

“Yep. You heard Sensei Ark talking about it too, didn’t you? About me. Ah… I was glad you remembered… I’m not the same as I was back then, but even so. Getting to see Sensei again through you—that made me happy.”
Talking about me? Whoever could that be?
“The demon child, I wonder?”
“Nope.”
“A child who’d get along well with me, the peeper?”
“Nope.”
“A serious child? Though rather feminine-seeming.”
“Nope. Are you doing this on purpose?”
Whoever could it be? Nothing was coming to mind.
“For my part, I really like that you chose not to build a harem. Though you did build yourself a bird family.”
Someone Ark talked about who built a harem…
“That fellow, the demon lord beast!”
“You really do get things wrong an endless number of times. Well, I have met him, at least.”
Apparently that wasn’t it either.

“Right, it’s a kid who had countless age-gap fiancées and, hating that, trained under Sensei Ark. More precisely, my partner had a connection to Sensei Ark who was teaching there, and through that I ended up being taught too. Along with Sensei Ark’s third-generation adopted child. We’d sneak up and touch absent-minded Sensei Ark’s back and train together, all of us. Got scolded something fierce afterward, I remember.”
Ah, yes, that story had come up before. I never imagined there was a connection.
“I was moved, through the spear, that Sensei Ark spoke with me here even though he probably couldn’t tell it was me.”
“Why can’t he speak with you now, I wonder?”

“Sensei Ark can no longer see spirits. Originally, I’m not quite human… no, that’s not right either. I’m what’s called a spirit-kind—a being that lives its first life half as a living creature, and upon death, lives a second life as a spirit.”
So such a race existed. One of those unique otherworldly settings, I supposed.
“In the end it’s close to, yet distant from, what becomes the Raph-species—a creature where, upon death, half becomes a spirit. The other half just goes around the normal cycle of reincarnation.”
“An odd race, I say.”
“Says the human who becomes a ghost when he dies?”

Hm… true enough. Ghosts and spirits—perhaps they really were close, after all. The idea that ancestral spirits watch over you seemed to connect to spirit worship too, come to think of it. There had been pigs back in my Japan who believed in such things, I recalled. Now that I thought of it, I even had memories of things like poltergeists.

“Long ago, Sensei Ark got angry over some unfairness that happened to us spirit-kind and helped out in various ways. That’s part of why so many spirits admire Sensei Ark. Well, back in those days, Sensei Ark was… saddled with a false accusation, though.”
So that was the reason the spirits were cooperative toward Ark. What a twist of fate, huh, the spirit of the spear murmured, nodding to itself.
“By the way, spirit-kind actually exist in this world too, though… well, that’s something you don’t need to know.”
“So then, spirit of the spear, what business do you have with me? I have no intention of quitting the loop, I say.”
“Ah, I knew you wouldn’t quit. Though after that last cycle, I did wonder whether you’d be all right after being dazed for a while.”
That cycle… gah, it was probably that cycle.
“You were relieved Filo wasn’t there, spaced out, dreading the next loop—and the other one was raring to go, so I was watching how things went.”
“The other one… Rival, I say! It’s parasitizing the spear!”
If the spirit could talk to me, then I should kick Rival out and create a Filo-tan folder.
“Throw that thing out, I say.”
At that, the spirit of the spear instantly shifted into Rival’s form.
“Nope, refused, nano—payback for turning her into a motorcycle axle, at least allow her this much, nano.”
“Don’t be ridiculous, I say! It’s parasitizing you!”

“Say what you like, but she’s well suited to steering you. In the end, she’ll be good at getting our voice through to you. And someone you adore has one too, don’t they—on the Shield side? Atla. Nano.”
Guh… so did that mean Rival had been chosen by the spirits to occupy the same position as Tiger Girl? Whatever taste they used to choose was terrible, I say.

“Speaking as a spirit, it’ll be hard to drag Filo into the loop. Well, since Sensei Ark and that crappy bird set things in motion, if you’re lucky you might eventually meet the original world’s Filo-chan again. Nano.”
“Don’t speak ill of Ho-kun, I say!”
“You’d call him a crappy bird too if you knew the inside story. Nano. That thing—should I call it a crappy bird, or more a sleep-trap bird? I was thoroughly put off. Nano.”
“Stop tacking on that forced ‘nano,’ I say!”
“Fufufu, nano.”
Gah… this spirit of the spear had a rather nasty personality. In my head, Father was pointing out that this was surely because I’d done terrible things like drive mode—but no, that wasn’t it!
“You should put up with a little, since I’m putting up with your selfishness. Nano.”
“Even so, I don’t like it, I say.”
“Then again, would you rather go back to the original Japan, forgetting everything up till now?”
“That would be far worse, I say!”
Exploiting my weakness like that—this spirit of the spear was the worst.
“The poison’s worn off of her too, and I wouldn’t suggest anything bad for you, so don’t worry about it.”
“I won’t forget that she seduced Father away from me, I say.”
“You could just steal him back, you know.”
“That would be disregarding Father’s own will, so that’s no good, I say.”
Father’s decisions were absolute, after all!
“How clumsy. I think stealing him back would be fine, don’t you? Hooray for men.”
“What are you even saying, you!?”

“Aren’t men wonderful? There’s a bond only men understand, born between men—and love can grow from that too. Ah, I’m like you, I swing both ways. Since we’re birds of a feather, let’s get along, shall we?”
What kind of mind did this spirit of the spear even have!? Was it perhaps twisted from some obsessive hatred of harems?
